$comment: Committed performance baseline. Regenerate with scripts/run-benchmarks.sh and commit
the change in a reviewed commit that states why the number moved — docs/21-Quality-Gates.md section 7.
Ratios here are computed the same way scripts/check-benchmark-budgets.py computes
them (relative to the fastest benchmark in the same report), NOT the way
BenchmarkDotNet's Ratio column does (relative to [Benchmark(Baseline = true)]).
Mixing the two bases spends the tolerance on a definitional difference instead of
allocatedBytes and ratioToBaseline are machine-independent and gated tightly.
absoluteNs is machine-dependent and gated loosely, as a catastrophe detector only.

recordedOn.note: Recorded in a container on shared hardware. Absolute figures are indicative; ratios and allocations are the contract.

DispatchBenchmarks.ViaReflection.note: Not a target. The comparison ADR-0002 rests on.

StepLoopBenchmarks.CompensateAll.note: Allocates today. WP-4 must pool it; AllocationBudgetTests carries the tripwire.

StepLoopBenchmarks.BuildPlan.note: Runs once per flow at startup, not per execution.
